claim: Neprilysins are highly conserved ectoenzymes that cleave and thereby inactivate many physiologically relevant peptides in the extracellular space.
source: Neprilysins are highly conserved ectoenzymes that cleave and thereby inactivate many physiologically relevant peptides in the extracellular space, thus contributing considerably to the maintenance of peptide homeostasis in this compartment.
evidence: This is a statement about the general function of neprilysins based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Members of the neprilysin family generally consist of a short N-terminal cytoplasmic domain, a membrane spanning region, and a large extracellular domain with two highly conserved sequence motifs (HExxH; ExxA/GD).
source: Members of the neprilysin family generally consist of a short N-terminal cytoplasmic domain, a membrane spanning region, and a large extracellular domain with two highly conserved sequence motifs (HExxH; ExxA/GD) critical for zinc coordination, catalysis, and substrate or inhibitor binding (Matthews, 1988; Oefner et al., 2000).
evidence: This structural information is supported by citations to Matthews, 1988 and Oefner et al., 2000.

claim: The conserved sequence motifs (HExxH; ExxA/GD) are critical for zinc coordination, catalysis, and substrate or inhibitor binding.
source: Members of the neprilysin family generally consist of a short N-terminal cytoplasmic domain, a membrane spanning region, and a large extracellular domain with two highly conserved sequence motifs (HExxH; ExxA/GD) critical for zinc coordination, catalysis, and substrate or inhibitor binding (Matthews, 1988; Oefner et al., 2000).
evidence: This functional information is supported by citations to Matthews, 1988 and Oefner et al., 2000.

claim: Neprilysins are classified as M13 zinc metallopeptidases.
source: Because of these characteristics, neprilysins are classified as M13 zinc metallopeptidases.
evidence: This is a classification statement based on established knowledge about neprilysin characteristics.

claim: Human Neprilysin (NEP) substrates include endothelins, angiotensins I and II, enkephalins, bradykinin, atrial natriuretic peptide, substance P, and the amyloid-beta peptide.
source: For human Neprilysin (NEP), the most well-characterized family member, identified substrates include endothelins, angiotensins I and II, enkephalins, bradykinin, atrial natriuretic peptide, substance P, and the amyloid-beta peptide (Turner et al., 2001).
evidence: This list of substrates is supported by citation to Turner et al., 2001.

claim: NEP activity has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
source: Because of this high substrate variability, NEP activity has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hypertension (Molinaro et al., 2002), analgesia (Whitworth, 2003), cancer (Turner et al., 2001), and Alzheimer's disease (Iwata et al., 2000; Belyaev et al., 2009).
evidence: This implication is supported by citation to Molinaro et al., 2002.

claim: NEP activity has been implicated in analgesia.
source: Because of this high substrate variability, NEP activity has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hypertension (Molinaro et al., 2002), analgesia (Whitworth, 2003), cancer (Turner et al., 2001), and Alzheimer's disease (Iwata et al., 2000; Belyaev et al., 2009).
evidence: This implication is supported by citation to Whitworth, 2003.

claim: NEP activity has been implicated in cancer.
source: Because of this high substrate variability, NEP activity has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hypertension (Molinaro et al., 2002), analgesia (Whitworth, 2003), cancer (Turner et al., 2001), and Alzheimer's disease (Iwata et al., 2000; Belyaev et al., 2009).
evidence: This implication is supported by citation to Turner et al., 2001.

claim: NEP activity has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease.
source: Because of this high substrate variability, NEP activity has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hypertension (Molinaro et al., 2002), analgesia (Whitworth, 2003), cancer (Turner et al., 2001), and Alzheimer's disease (Iwata et al., 2000; Belyaev et al., 2009).
evidence: This implication is supported by citations to Iwata et al., 2000 and Belyaev et al., 2009.

claim: Recent clinical trials have demonstrated significant efficacy of Neprilysin inhibitors in the treatment of certain indications.
source: Recent clinical trials have demonstrated significant efficacy of Neprilysin inhibitors in the treatment of certain indications (Jessup, 2014; McMurray et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jessup, 2014 and McMurray et al., 2014.

claim: At least five neprilysin genes are expressed in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: In Drosophila melanogaster, at least five neprilysin genes are expressed (Meyer et al., 2011; Sitnik et al., 2014), two of the corresponding protein products, Nep2 and Nep4, were reported to be enzymatically active (Bland et al., 2007; Meyer et al., 2009; Thomas et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Meyer et al., 2011 and Sitnik et al., 2014.

claim: Nep2 and Nep4 were reported to be enzymatically active.
source: In Drosophila melanogaster, at least five neprilysin genes are expressed (Meyer et al., 2011; Sitnik et al., 2014), two of the corresponding protein products, Nep2 and Nep4, were reported to be enzymatically active (Bland et al., 2007; Meyer et al., 2009; Thomas et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bland et al., 2007, Meyer et al., 2009, and Thomas et al., 2005.

claim: The intracellular N-terminus of Nep4 has a critical function, and when present in excess, induces severe muscle degeneration concomitant with lethality during late larval development.
source: With respect to Nep4, a critical function of the enzyme's non-catalytic intracellular N-terminus has been demonstrated: when present in excess, the domain induces severe muscle degeneration concomitant with lethality during late larval development.
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings, implicitly referencing prior work.

claim: The intracellular domain of Nep4 interacts with a carbohydrate kinase.
source: Because the intracellular domain interacts with a carbohydrate kinase, impaired energy metabolism has been proposed as the underlying cause of the phenotype (Panz et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Panz et al., 2012.

claim: Impaired energy metabolism has been proposed as the underlying cause of the muscle degeneration phenotype induced by excess Nep4 intracellular domain.
source: Because the intracellular domain interacts with a carbohydrate kinase, impaired energy metabolism has been proposed as the underlying cause of the phenotype (Panz et al., 2012).
evidence: This proposal is supported by citation to Panz et al., 2012.

claim: Nep2 has been implicated in the regulation of locomotion and geotactic behavior.
source: In addition, Nep2 has been implicated in the regulation of locomotion and geotactic behavior (Bland et al., 2009), and neprilysin activity in general appears to be critical to the formation of middle- and long-term memory (Turrel et al., 2016), as well as to the regulation of pigment dispersing factor (PDF) signaling within circadian neural circuits (Isaac et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bland et al., 2009.

claim: Neprilysin activity appears to be critical to the formation of middle- and long-term memory.
source: In addition, Nep2 has been implicated in the regulation of locomotion and geotactic behavior (Bland et al., 2009), and neprilysin activity in general appears to be critical to the formation of middle- and long-term memory (Turrel et al., 2016), as well as to the regulation of pigment dispersing factor (PDF) signaling within circadian neural circuits (Isaac et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Turrel et al., 2016.

claim: Neprilysin activity appears to be critical to the regulation of pigment dispersing factor (PDF) signaling within circadian neural circuits.
source: In addition, Nep2 has been implicated in the regulation of locomotion and geotactic behavior (Bland et al., 2009), and neprilysin activity in general appears to be critical to the formation of middle- and long-term memory (Turrel et al., 2016), as well as to the regulation of pigment dispersing factor (PDF) signaling within circadian neural circuits (Isaac et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Isaac et al., 2007.

claim: Neprilysins have a critical role in reproduction.
source: However, despite these experiments and recent findings that suggest a critical role of neprilysins in reproduction (Sitnik et al., 2014), the physiological functionality of these enzymes is still far from being understood.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sitnik et al., 2014.

claim: Nep4 is expressed in larval body wall muscles.
source: In previous experiments, we showed that Nep4 is expressed in larval body wall muscles and that increased expression of the peptidase in this tissue interferes with muscle function and integrity and severely impairs movement of the larvae (Panz et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Panz et al., 2012.

claim: Increased expression of Nep4 in muscle tissue interferes with muscle function and integrity and severely impairs movement of the larvae.
source: In previous experiments, we showed that Nep4 is expressed in larval body wall muscles and that increased expression of the peptidase in this tissue interferes with muscle function and integrity and severely impairs movement of the larvae (Panz et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Panz et al., 2012.

claim: An increase in Nep4A in muscle cells (mef2-Gal4 driver) induced biphasic lethality with an early phase occurring throughout embryonic and early larval development, and a late phase evident by the end of larval development.
source: In the present study, we found that an increase in Nep4A in muscle cells (mef2-Gal4 driver) also induced biphasic lethality. An early phase occurred throughout embryonic and early larval development, and a late phase was evident by the end of larval development (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Early lethality was observed only upon overexpression of the active enzyme; expression of catalytically inactive Nep4A did not affect viability at this point of development.
source: Significantly, early lethality was observed only upon overexpression of the active enzyme; expression of catalytically inactive Nep4A, carrying a glutamine instead of an essential glutamate (E873Q) within the zinc-binding motif, did not affect viability at this point of development.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations comparing active and inactive Nep4A constructs.

claim: Overexpression of catalytically active or inactive Nep4A constructs induced late larval lethality.
source: By contrast, overexpression of catalytically active or inactive Nep4A constructs induced late larval lethality.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations.

claim: Lethality during early development is caused exclusively by a detrimental increase in catalytic activity.
source: These distinct effects demonstrate that lethality during early development is caused exclusively by a detrimental increase in catalytic activity, whereas late larval lethality appears to be a consequence of multiple physiological impairments.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential effects of active vs. inactive Nep4A on early lethality.

claim: Late larval lethality appears to be a consequence of multiple physiological impairments.
source: These distinct effects demonstrate that lethality during early development is caused exclusively by a detrimental increase in catalytic activity, whereas late larval lethality appears to be a consequence of multiple physiological impairments.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that both active and inactive Nep4A induce late larval lethality.

claim: Muscle-specific knockdown of nep4 slightly increased embryonic mortality.
source: Muscle-specific knockdown of nep4 slightly increased embryonic mortality, but the majority of the respective animals died during metamorphosis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The majority of nep4 knockdown animals died during metamorphosis.
source: Muscle-specific knockdown of nep4 slightly increased embryonic mortality, but the majority of the respective animals died during metamorphosis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Simultaneous overexpression of Nep4A completely rescued the RNAi phenotypes (embryonic/pupal lethality), thus confirming specificity of the knockdown.
source: To confirm RNAi specificity, we also analyzed flies expressing both the respective RNAi construct as well as the Nep4A overexpression construct. Simultaneous overexpression of Nep4A completely rescued the RNAi phenotypes (embryonic/pupal lethality), thus confirming specificity of the knockdown (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A demonstrating rescue of RNAi phenotypes.

claim: mef2 is expressed in distinct neurons, including clock neurons and Kenyon cells.
source: As shown previously, in addition to muscle tissue mef2 is expressed in distinct neurons, including clock neurons (Blanchard, 2010) and Kenyon cells (Schulz et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Blanchard, 2010 and Schulz et al., 1996.

claim: Pan-neuronal overexpression or knockdown of nep4 (using elav-Gal4 driver) had no significant influence on viability.
source: To determine whether the effects described above (using mef2-Gal4 as a driver) are exclusively based on Nep4 activity in muscles, or if neuronal Nep4 is also involved, we used pan-neuronal elav-Gal4 as a driver to increase or reduce nep4 expression. In this line of experiments, neither overexpression nor knockdown of nep4 had any significant influence on viability (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The effects observed with mef2-Gal4 are muscle-specific.
source: This result indicates that the effects observed with mef2-Gal4 are muscle-specific.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lack of effect with neuronal-specific driver.

claim: Nep4 is expressed in glial cells of the central nervous system (CNS).
source: In addition to muscle tissue, Nep4 is also expressed in glial cells of the central nervous system (CNS) (Meyer et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Meyer et al., 2009.

claim: Neither increased nor reduced nep4 expression in glial cells significantly affected life span.
source: However, in contrast to the effects observed in muscle cells, neither increased nor reduced nep4 expression in glial cells, using glia-specific repo-Gal4 as a driver, significantly affected life span (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Muscle-specific overexpression of the active enzyme decreased the size and weight of third instar larvae relative to control animals.
source: In third instar larvae, muscle-specific overexpression of the active enzyme decreased the size and weight of the animals relative to control animals, whereas overexpression of catalytically inactive Nep4A did not affect size or weight.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental measurements of size and weight.

claim: Overexpression of catalytically inactive Nep4A did not affect size or weight of third instar larvae.
source: In third instar larvae, muscle-specific overexpression of the active enzyme decreased the size and weight of the animals relative to control animals, whereas overexpression of catalytically inactive Nep4A did not affect size or weight.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental measurements of size and weight.

claim: Knockdown of the peptidase in muscle tissue did not significantly alter size or weight parameters.
source: Knockdown of the peptidase in the same tissue did also not significantly alter these parameters (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Increased nep4A expression in glial cells or neurons did not affect the size or weight of the larvae.
source: In contrast to the muscle-specific effects, increased nep4A expression in glial cells or neurons did not affect the size or weight of the larvae.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental measurements.

claim: Glial cell specific nep4 knockdown slightly reduced size and weight.
source: Glial cell specific nep4 knockdown slightly reduced both parameters, whereas neuronal knockdown had no effect (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Neuronal knockdown of nep4 had no effect on size or weight.
source: Glial cell specific nep4 knockdown slightly reduced both parameters, whereas neuronal knockdown had no effect (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The effects of nep4 knockdown on size and weight were completely rescued by simultaneous overexpression of Nep4A, which confirms specificity of the respective RNAi construct.
source: In line with the lethality assay, the effects of nep4 knockdown on size and weight were completely rescued by simultaneous overexpression of Nep4A, which again confirms specificity of the respective RNAi construct.
evidence: This claim is based on rescue experiments demonstrating RNAi specificity.

claim: Nep4 has essential functions in muscle tissue and glial cells.
source: The depicted results indicate essential functions of Nep4 in muscle tissue and glial cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the various phenotypic effects observed.

claim: The effects of modifying nep4 expression were more severe in muscles, suggesting the active enzyme has a critical function particularly in this tissue.
source: However, the effects of modifying nep4 expression were more severe in muscles, suggesting the active enzyme has a critical function particularly in this tissue.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the severity of effects across different tissues.

claim: Increasing or decreasing the expression of nep4 in muscle tissue affected metabolite concentrations in transgenic third instar larvae.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, increasing or decreasing the expression of nep4 in muscle tissue affected metabolite concentrations in transgenic third instar larvae.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR metabolomics data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Knockdown of nep4 increased the levels of fructose and a purine.
source: Knockdown of nep4 increased the levels of fructose and a purine and decreased the levels of NAD, a purine nucleotide, and glutamine (Figure 2B,C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR metabolomics data shown in Figure 2B, 2C, and source data 1.

claim: Knockdown of nep4 decreased the levels of NAD, a purine nucleotide, and glutamine.
source: Knockdown of nep4 increased the levels of fructose and a purine and decreased the levels of NAD, a purine nucleotide, and glutamine (Figure 2B,C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR metabolomics data shown in Figure 2B, 2C, and source data 1.

claim: Nep4A overexpression increased the signals of histidine, glutamine, and a purine.
source: Nep4A overexpression increased the signals of histidine, glutamine, and the same purine.
evidence: This claim is based on NMR metabolomics data.

claim: Nep4A overexpression resulted in a significant increase in the spectral regions specific to glucose and fructose, indicating elevated levels of the two monosaccharides.
source: In addition, a significant increase was observed in the spectral regions specific to glucose and fructose, indicating elevated levels of the two monosaccharides.
evidence: This claim is based on NMR metabolomics data.

claim: Lactate, NAD, trehalose, and tyrosine concentrations were reduced in Nep4A-overexpressing animals.
source: On the other hand, lactate, NAD, trehalose, and tyrosine concentrations were reduced in Nep4A-overexpressing animals (Figure 2B,C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR metabolomics data shown in Figure 2B, 2C, and source data 1.

claim: Increased formation of lactate and NAD is a hallmark of aerobic glycolysis.
source: Of note, increased formation of lactate and NAD is a hallmark of aerobic glycolysis, a specific metabolic program that starts approximately 12 hr before the end of embryogenesis.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about aerobic glycolysis.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis is a specific metabolic program that starts approximately 12 hr before the end of embryogenesis.
source: Of note, increased formation of lactate and NAD is a hallmark of aerobic glycolysis, a specific metabolic program that starts approximately 12 hr before the end of embryogenesis.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about Drosophila development.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis enables hatched 1st instar larvae to efficiently convert dietary carbohydrates into biomass, thereby supporting the considerable increase in body mass that occurs during larval development.
source: Aerobic glycolysis enables hatched 1st instar larvae to efficiently convert dietary carbohydrates into biomass, thereby supporting the considerable increase in body mass that occurs during larval development (Tennessen et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tennessen et al., 2014.

claim: Inhibition of aerobic glycolysis in the course of the larval growth phase prevents the animals from metabolizing sufficient quantities of sugar, resulting in larval lethality.
source: Inhibition of aerobic glycolysis in the course of this growth phase prevents the animals from metabolizing sufficient quantities of sugar, resulting in larval lethality (Tennessen et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tennessen et al., 2011.

claim: Animals overexpressing Nep4A die primarily during the embryonic-larval transition and during larval development.
source: The fact that animals overexpressing Nep4A die primarily during the embryonic-larval transition and during larval development (Figure 1A) and exhibit considerably reduced lactate and NAD levels indicates that an excess of Nep4A may interfere with this distinct metabolic program.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: An excess of Nep4A may interfere with aerobic glycolysis.
source: The fact that animals overexpressing Nep4A die primarily during the embryonic-larval transition and during larval development (Figure 1A) and exhibit considerably reduced lactate and NAD levels indicates that an excess of Nep4A may interfere with this distinct metabolic program.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the timing of lethality and metabolic changes.

claim: Transgenes overexpressing the peptidase were characterized by considerably reduced food intake.
source: As depicted in Figure 3A, transgenes overexpressing the peptidase were characterized by considerably reduced food intake.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: After 10 min of feeding, Nep4A overexpressing animals had ingested 47% less food than controls.
source: After 10 min of feeding, the respective animals had ingested 47% less food than controls, after 20 min 59.5% less, and after 40 min 57% less, relative to controls.
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative feeding assay data.

claim: After 20 min of feeding, Nep4A overexpressing animals had ingested 59.5% less food than controls.
source: After 10 min of feeding, the respective animals had ingested 47% less food than controls, after 20 min 59.5% less, and after 40 min 57% less, relative to controls.
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative feeding assay data.

claim: After 40 min of feeding, Nep4A overexpressing animals had ingested 57% less food than controls.
source: After 10 min of feeding, the respective animals had ingested 47% less food than controls, after 20 min 59.5% less, and after 40 min 57% less, relative to controls.
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative feeding assay data.

claim: nep4 knockdown did not affect food intake after 40 min.
source: By contrast, nep4 knockdown did not affect food intake after 40 min; however, corresponding animals were characterized by significantly reduced food intake after 10 min (47% of control intake) and 20 min (72% of control intake), indicating a delayed initiation of feeding.
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative feeding assay data.

claim: nep4 knockdown animals were characterized by significantly reduced food intake after 10 min (47% of control intake) and 20 min (72% of control intake), indicating a delayed initiation of feeding.
source: By contrast, nep4 knockdown did not affect food intake after 40 min; however, corresponding animals were characterized by significantly reduced food intake after 10 min (47% of control intake) and 20 min (72% of control intake), indicating a delayed initiation of feeding.
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative feeding assay data and includes an interpretation.

claim: Overexpression of catalytically inactive Nep4A did not affect food intake.
source: To investigate the possibility that the observed effects were caused by protein properties other than enzymatic activity, we also analyzed catalytically inactive Nep4A. Significantly, overexpression of this construct did not affect food intake, thus confirming abnormal catalytic activity as a causative factor (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Abnormal catalytic activity is a causative factor for the observed effects on food intake.
source: To investigate the possibility that the observed effects were caused by protein properties other than enzymatic activity, we also analyzed catalytically inactive Nep4A. Significantly, overexpression of this construct did not affect food intake, thus confirming abnormal catalytic activity as a causative factor (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lack of effect with catalytically inactive Nep4A.

claim: Increased glucose levels in Nep4A overexpression animals are symptomatic of impaired insulin signaling.
source: Since the increased glucose levels that are evident in Nep4A overexpression animals (Figure 2B,C) are symptomatic of impaired insulin signaling (Broughton et al., 2005; Rulifson et al., 2002), in a continuative set of experiments we analyzed whether altering nep4 levels also affected the expression of Drosophila insulin-like peptides (dilps).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Broughton et al., 2005 and Rulifson et al., 2002.

claim: dilps 1, 2, 3, and 5 encode the major insulin-like peptides expressed by larval insulin-producing cells (IPCs).
source: We focused on dilps 1, 2, 3, and 5 because they encode the major insulin-like peptides expressed by larval insulin-producing cells (IPCs) (Rulifson et al., 2002; Brogiolo et al., 2001; Cao and Brown, 2001; Ikeya et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2008; Nässel et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: IPCs are located within the median neurosecretory cell cluster of the central brain.
source: IPCs are located within the median neurosecretory cell cluster of the central brain and apparently function like pancreatic β-cells, since IPC ablation in Drosophila results in elevated levels of circulating glucose.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about Drosophila IPCs.

claim: IPCs apparently function like pancreatic β-cells.
source: IPCs are located within the median neurosecretory cell cluster of the central brain and apparently function like pancreatic β-cells, since IPC ablation in Drosophila results in elevated levels of circulating glucose.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional similarity.

claim: IPC ablation in Drosophila results in elevated levels of circulating glucose.
source: IPCs are located within the median neurosecretory cell cluster of the central brain and apparently function like pancreatic β-cells, since IPC ablation in Drosophila results in elevated levels of circulating glucose. In addition, animals with ablated IPCs are smaller than wild-type specimens, and they weigh less (Broughton et al., 2005; Rulifson et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Broughton et al., 2005 and Rulifson et al., 2002.

claim: Animals with ablated IPCs are smaller than wild-type specimens, and they weigh less.
source: In addition, animals with ablated IPCs are smaller than wild-type specimens, and they weigh less (Broughton et al., 2005; Rulifson et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Broughton et al., 2005 and Rulifson et al., 2002.

claim: Muscle-specific Nep4A overexpression phenocopied characteristic effects of IPC ablation, including reduced size and weight of corresponding animals, as well as increased levels of carbohydrates such as glucose and fructose.
source: Significantly, these characteristic effects of IPC ablation were phenocopied by muscle-specific Nep4A overexpression (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of phenotypes shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Nep4A-overexpressing animals exhibited considerably reduced expression of dilps 1, 2, 3, and 5.
source: Furthermore, the respective transgenic animals exhibited considerably reduced expression of the selected dilps. In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp1 expression decreased by 59%, dilp2 by 83%, dilp3 expression by 88%, and dilp5 expression by 84%, relative to expression in controls.
evidence: This claim is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp1 expression decreased by 59%.
source: In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp1 expression decreased by 59%, dilp2 by 83%, dilp3 expression by 88%, and dilp5 expression by 84%, relative to expression in controls.
evidence: This claim is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp2 expression decreased by 83%.
source: In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp1 expression decreased by 59%, dilp2 by 83%, dilp3 expression by 88%, and dilp5 expression by 84%, relative to expression in controls.
evidence: This claim is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp3 expression decreased by 88%.
source: In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp1 expression decreased by 59%, dilp2 by 83%, dilp3 expression by 88%, and dilp5 expression by 84%, relative to expression in controls.
evidence: This claim is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp5 expression decreased by 84%.
source: In Nep4A-overexpressing animals, dilp1 expression decreased by 59%, dilp2 by 83%, dilp3 expression by 88%, and dilp5 expression by 84%, relative to expression in controls.
evidence: This claim is based on qRT-PCR data.

claim: Muscle-specific nep4 knockdown had no effect on the expression of dilps 1, 3, and 5.
source: On the other hand, muscle-specific nep4 knockdown had no effect on the expression of dilps 1, 3, and 5, although expression of dilp2 increased by 82%, relative to expression in controls (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Muscle-specific nep4 knockdown increased expression of dilp2 by 82%.
source: On the other hand, muscle-specific nep4 knockdown had no effect on the expression of dilps 1, 3, and 5, although expression of dilp2 increased by 82%, relative to expression in controls (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The rather mild effect of nep4 knockdown on dilp expression, when compared to the effects of Nep4A overexpression, suggests that other, yet unknown peptidases can compensate for reduced Nep4 activity.
source: The rather mild effect of nep4 knockdown on dilp expression, when compared to the effects of Nep4A overexpression, suggests that other, yet unknown peptidases can compensate for reduced Nep4 activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential effects of overexpression vs. knockdown.

claim: dilp expression is only affected by the wild type enzyme, while overexpression of catalytically inactive Nep4A did not significantly alter expression of the selected dilps.
source: In line with the results from the feeding assay (Figure 3A), dilp expression is only affected by the wild type enzyme, while overexpression of catalytically inactive Nep4A did not significantly alter expression of the selected dilps (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Glial-cell-specific overexpression of Nep4A increased the expression of dilp5.
source: As depicted in Figure 3—figure supplement 1, glial-cell-specific overexpression of Nep4A increased the expression of dilp5, while nep4 knockdown in the same cells resulted in an upregulation of dilp2 and downregulation of dilp3.
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Glial-cell-specific nep4 knockdown resulted in an upregulation of dilp2 and downregulation of dilp3.
source: As depicted in Figure 3—figure supplement 1, glial-cell-specific overexpression of Nep4A increased the expression of dilp5, while nep4 knockdown in the same cells resulted in an upregulation of dilp2 and downregulation of dilp3.
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Proper regulation of dilp expression requires adequate Nep4 levels within the CNS.
source: Although these effects were minor compared to the effects of modulating the expression of muscle-bound Nep4 (Figure 3B), they demonstrate that proper regulation of dilp expression also requires adequate Nep4 levels within the CNS.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effects of CNS-specific Nep4 modulation.

claim: In body wall muscles, Nep4 exhibits a dual localization: to membranes continuous with the nuclear membrane and to the surface of the muscles.
source: As depicted in Figure 4, in body wall muscles Nep4 exhibits a dual localization: in addition to localizing to membranes continuous with the nuclear membrane (Figure 4A, arrowheads), which we previously identified as related to the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum (Panz et al., 2012), the peptidase accumulates at the surface of the muscles (Figure 4A, arrows).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Membranes continuous with the nuclear membrane in body wall muscles were previously identified as related to the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum.
source: As depicted in Figure 4, in body wall muscles Nep4 exhibits a dual localization: in addition to localizing to membranes continuous with the nuclear membrane (Figure 4A, arrowheads), which we previously identified as related to the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum (Panz et al., 2012), the peptidase accumulates at the surface of the muscles (Figure 4A, arrows).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Panz et al., 2012.

claim: Nep4 localization at the surface of muscles is consistent with ectoenzymatic activity and indicative of a function in regulating the homeostasis of hemolymph circulating peptides.
source: The latter localization is consistent with ectoenzymatic activity and indicative of a function in regulating the homeostasis of hemolymph circulating peptides.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the surface localization of Nep4.

claim: The proteins expressed from the two overexpression constructs (wild-type Nep4A and catalytically inactive Nep4A) exhibited subcellular localizations identical to that of the endogenous protein.
source: Of note, the proteins expressed from the two overexpression constructs (wild-type Nep4A and catalytically inactive Nep4A) exhibited subcellular localizations identical to that of the endogenous protein (Figure 4A,D,F), confirming that the observed overexpression phenotypes (Figures 1–3) were not impaired by mislocalization of the respective constructs.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The observed overexpression phenotypes were not impaired by mislocalization of the respective constructs.
source: Of note, the proteins expressed from the two overexpression constructs (wild-type Nep4A and catalytically inactive Nep4A) exhibited subcellular localizations identical to that of the endogenous protein (Figure 4A,D,F), confirming that the observed overexpression phenotypes (Figures 1–3) were not impaired by mislocalization of the respective constructs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the proper localization of overexpressed constructs.

claim: Brain and ventral nerve cord tissue exhibited substantial nep4 reporter gene expression.
source: As shown in Figure 5, brain and ventral nerve cord tissue exhibited substantial reporter gene expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter gene expression data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In the brain, nep4 expression was observed mainly in lamina and central brain cells, while only a few medulla cells exhibited a distinct signal.
source: With respect to the brain, expression was observed mainly in lamina (Figure 5A, brackets) and central brain cells (Figure 5A, dashed line), while only a few medulla cells exhibited a distinct signal (Figure 5A, bar).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter gene expression data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Within the ventral nerve cord, nep4 was detected in numerous cells along all segments.
source: Within the ventral nerve cord, nep4 was detected in numerous cells along all segments.
evidence: This claim is based on reporter gene expression data.

claim: nep4 was expressed primarily in glial cells.
source: As confirmed by extensive colocalization with the glial cell marker Reversed-polarity (Repo), nep4 was expressed primarily in this cell type; however, especially in the median region of the central brain, only partial colocalization was evident.
evidence: This claim is based on colocalization data with glial cell marker.

claim: In addition to glial cells, nep4 is expressed in certain neurons of the central brain.
source: Thus, in addition to glial cells, nep4 is expressed in certain neurons of the central brain (Figure 5A-C).
evidence: This claim is based on partial colocalization with glial marker shown in Figure 5.

claim: nep4 is expressed in all IPCs.
source: Interestingly, as confirmed by colocalization with dilp2-specific reporter gene expression, we found that these neurons included all IPCs, which reside within the median neurosecretory cell cluster of the brain hemispheres.
evidence: This claim is based on colocalization data with dilp2 reporter.

claim: IPCs reside within the median neurosecretory cell cluster of the brain hemispheres.
source: Interestingly, as confirmed by colocalization with dilp2-specific reporter gene expression, we found that these neurons included all IPCs, which reside within the median neurosecretory cell cluster of the brain hemispheres.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about IPC location.

claim: Nep4 accumulated at the surface of numerous cells of the central brain, including IPCs.
source: As depicted in Figure 6D–F, the peptidase accumulated at the surface of numerous cells of the central brain, including IPCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6D-F.

claim: Major phenotypes described in this study strictly depend on the catalytic activity of Nep4.
source: The fact that major phenotypes described in this study strictly depend on the catalytic activity of Nep4 (Figures 1 and 3) indicates that aberrant hydrolysis of peptides involved in regulating dilp expression and / or feeding behavior is primarily responsible for the phenotypes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential effects of active vs. inactive Nep4A.

claim: Aberrant hydrolysis of peptides involved in regulating dilp expression and/or feeding behavior is primarily responsible for the phenotypes.
source: The fact that major phenotypes described in this study strictly depend on the catalytic activity of Nep4 (Figures 1 and 3) indicates that aberrant hydrolysis of peptides involved in regulating dilp expression and / or feeding behavior is primarily responsible for the phenotypes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the catalytic activity dependence of phenotypes.

claim: IPCs constitute the major site of Dilp synthesis in Drosophila.
source: This indication is corroborated by the localization of Nep4 to the surface of body wall muscles and IPCs (Figures 4 and 6), with the latter constituting the major site of Dilp synthesis in Drosophila (Rulifson et al., 2002; Brogiolo et al., 2001; Ikeya et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rulifson et al., 2002, Brogiolo et al., 2001, and Ikeya et al., 2002.

claim: 16 out of 23 candidate peptides were hydrolyzed at distinct positions by purified Nep4.
source: As depicted in Table 1, we found 23 peptides matching these criteria. Among these candidates, 16 were hydrolyzed at distinct positions by purified Nep4, while the remaining seven peptides were not significantly cleaved.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 1.

claim: The identified Nep4 substrates were adipokinetic hormone (AKH), allatostatin A1-4, corazonin, diuretic hormone 31 (DH31), drosulfakinins 1 and 2, leucokinin, short neuropeptide F11–11, short neuropeptide F14–11, and tachykinins 1, 2, 4, and 5.
source: The identified substrates were adipokinetic hormone (AKH), allatostatin A1-4, corazonin, diuretic hormone 31 (DH31), drosulfakinins 1 and 2, leucokinin, short neuropeptide F11–11, short neuropeptide F14–11 (also corresponding to sNPF212–19), and tachykinins 1, 2, 4, and 5.
evidence: This claim is based on mass spectrometry analysis of peptide cleavage.

claim: No Nep4-specific cleavage was observed for hugin, neuropeptide F, proctolin, short neuropeptide F3, short neuropeptide F4, and tachykinins 3 and 6.
source: No Nep4-specific cleavage was observed for hugin, neuropeptide F, proctolin, short neuropeptide F3, short neuropeptide F4, and tachykinins 3 and 6.
evidence: This claim is based on mass spectrometry analysis showing no cleavage.

claim: Nep4 preferentially cleaved next to hydrophobic residues, particularly with Phe or Leu at P1´.
source: Analysis of the resulting hydrolysis products revealed that Nep4 preferentially cleaved next to hydrophobic residues, particularly with Phe or Leu at P1´ (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of cleavage sites shown in Table 1.

claim: Identically treated control preparations lacking the peptidase did not exhibit any cleavage activity.
source: Identically treated control preparations lacking the peptidase did not exhibit any cleavage activity (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by control mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Modulating the expression of a Drosophila neprilysin interferes with the expression of insulin-like peptides, thus establishing a correlation between neprilysin activity and the regulation of insulin signaling.
source: This study demonstrates that modulating the expression of a Drosophila neprilysin interferes with the expression of insulin-like peptides, thus establishing a correlation between neprilysin activity and the regulation of insulin signaling.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main finding based on experimental data.

claim: Altering nep4 expression phenocopies characteristic effects of IPC ablation, including reduced size and weight of corresponding animals, as well as increased levels of carbohydrates such as glucose and fructose.
source: A high physiological relevance is confirmed by the fact that altering nep4 expression phenocopies characteristic effects of IPC ablation, including reduced size and weight of corresponding animals, as well as increased levels of carbohydrates such as glucose and fructose (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of phenotypes shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The increased levels of glucose and fructose, although food intake rates are reduced, presumably reflects the physiological impact of the diminished ilp expression.
source: The result that the levels of these sugars are increased, although food intake rates are reduced (Figure 3A) presumably reflects the physiological impact of the diminished ilp expression that is also obvious in corresponding animals (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the metabolic and expression data.

claim: The impaired insulin signaling likely results in inefficient metabolization and thus accumulation of the sugars, which overcompensates the diametrical effects of reduced food intake.
source: In this respect, the impaired insulin signaling likely results in inefficient metabolization and thus accumulation of the sugars, which overcompensates the diametrical effects of reduced food intake.
evidence: This is an inference drawn to explain the metabolic observations.

claim: Neprilysin-mediated hydrolysis of hemolymph circulating as well as CNS intrinsic peptides is the physiological basis of the described phenotypes.
source: By identifying 16 novel peptide substrates of Nep4, the majority of which are involved in regulating dilp expression or feeding behavior (Table 1, Figure 7), and by localizing the peptidase to the surface of body wall muscles (Figure 4) and IPCs within the larval CNS (Figure 6), we provide initial evidence that neprilysin-mediated hydrolysis of hemolymph circulating as well as CNS intrinsic peptides is the physiological basis of the described phenotypes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the substrate identification and localization data.

claim: Only the catalytically active enzyme affected dilp expression whereas the inactive construct did not, which confirms aberrant enzymatic activity and thus abnormal peptide hydrolysis as a causative parameter.
source: The finding that only the catalytically active enzyme affected dilp expression whereas the inactive construct did not (Figure 3B), substantiates this evidence because it confirms aberrant enzymatic activity and thus abnormal peptide hydrolysis as a causative parameter.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential effects of active vs. inactive enzyme.

claim: The strongest effects on size and dilp expression were observed with muscle-specific overexpression of Nep4.
source: Interestingly, we observed the strongest effects on size and dilp expression with muscle-specific overexpression of Nep4; overexpression of the peptidase in the CNS was less detrimental (Figure 1, Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of effects across different tissues.

claim: Hemolymph circulating peptides accessible to muscle-bound Nep4 are mainly responsible for the observed effects, while CNS intrinsic peptide signaling is less relevant.
source: These results indicate that hemolymph circulating peptides accessible to muscle-bound Nep4 are mainly responsible for the observed effects, while CNS intrinsic peptide signaling is less relevant.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the tissue-specific effects.

claim: All peptides cleaved by Nep4 could be released into the hemolymph, either from enteroendocrine cells or from neurohormonal release sites.
source: The fact that all peptides cleaved by Nep4 (Table 1) could be released into the hemolymph, either from enteroendocrine cells or from neurohormonal release sites (Nässel and Winther, 2010), substantiates this indication.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nässel and Winther, 2010.

claim: The Drosophila midgut is the source of several neuropeptides.
source: Since the Drosophila midgut is the source of several neuropeptides (Veenstra et al., 2008; Reiher et al., 2011), it is conceivable that a main reason for the observed phenotypes is aberrant cleavage of certain gut-derived peptides that are required for proper midgut-IPC communication.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Veenstra et al., 2008 and Reiher et al., 2011.

claim: Allatostatin A, neuropeptide F, diuretic hormone 31, and some tachykinins are produced by endocrine cells of the gut.
source: Allatostatin A, neuropeptide F, diuretic hormone 31, and some tachykinins are produced by endocrine cells of the gut (Veenstra et al., 2008; Reiher et al., 2011; Lenz et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Veenstra et al., 2008, Reiher et al., 2011, and Lenz et al., 2001.

claim: Allatostatin A, neuropeptide F, diuretic hormone 31, and tachykinins have been implicated in regulating dilp expression and/or feeding behavior.
source: Interestingly, all have been implicated in regulating dilp expression and/or feeding behavior (Nässel et al., 2013; Pool and Scott, 2014), and most of them, namely allatostatin A1-4, diuretic hormone 31, and tachykinin 1, 2, 4, and 5, were cleaved by Nep4 (Table 1), indicating enzyme-substrate relationships.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nässel et al., 2013 and Pool and Scott, 2014.

claim: Allatostatin A1-4, diuretic hormone 31, and tachykinin 1, 2, 4, and 5 were cleaved by Nep4, indicating enzyme-substrate relationships.
source: Interestingly, all have been implicated in regulating dilp expression and/or feeding behavior (Nässel et al., 2013; Pool and Scott, 2014), and most of them, namely allatostatin A1-4, diuretic hormone 31, and tachykinin 1, 2, 4, and 5, were cleaved by Nep4 (Table 1), indicating enzyme-substrate relationships.
evidence: This claim is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Table 1.

claim: Nep4 activity at the surface of muscle cells is necessary to maintain homeostasis of distinct hemolymph circulating signaling peptides, probably gut-derived, thereby ensuring proper midgut-IPC communication.
source: Thus, these results suggest that Nep4 activity at the surface of muscle cells is necessary to maintain homeostasis of distinct hemolymph circulating signaling peptides, probably gut-derived, thereby ensuring proper midgut-IPC communication.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the substrate identification and localization data.

claim: Unpaired 2, DILP6, and Stunted are known to mediate fat body-IPC feedback.
source: However, the only factors known to mediate this process, Unpaired 2 (Rajan and Perrimon, 2012), DILP6 (Bai et al., 2012), and Stunted (Delanoue et al., 2016﻿) have molecular masses of more than 5 kDa, and thus exceed the maximum mass of a putative neprilysin substrate (Oefner et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rajan and Perrimon, 2012, Bai et al., 2012, and Delanoue et al., 2016.

claim: Unpaired 2, DILP6, and Stunted have molecular masses of more than 5 kDa, and thus exceed the maximum mass of a putative neprilysin substrate.
source: However, the only factors known to mediate this process, Unpaired 2 (Rajan and Perrimon, 2012), DILP6 (Bai et al., 2012), and Stunted (Delanoue et al., 2016﻿) have molecular masses of more than 5 kDa, and thus exceed the maximum mass of a putative neprilysin substrate (Oefner et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is based on known molecular masses and citation to Oefner et al., 2000 for substrate size limit.

claim: A direct regulatory influence of Nep4 on Unpaired 2, DILP6, or Stunted activity appears unlikely.
source: Consequently, a direct regulatory influence of Nep4 on Unpaired 2, DILP6, or Stunted activity appears unlikely.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the size constraint.

claim: nep4 is expressed in numerous cells of the central nervous system, predominantly in glial cells.
source: In addition to body wall muscles, nep4 is expressed in numerous cells of the central nervous system, predominantly in glial cells (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter gene expression data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Modulating nep4 expression in glial cells has distinct and less severe effects on dilp expression compared to the muscle-specific effects.
source: Interestingly, compared to the muscle-specific effects, modulating nep4 expression in this tissue has distinct and less severe effects on dilp expression (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of qRT-PCR data across tissues.

claim: CNS intrinsic Nep4 activity affects different neuropeptide regulatory systems than the corresponding muscle-bound activity.
source: This result suggests that CNS intrinsic Nep4 activity affects different neuropeptide regulatory systems than the corresponding muscle-bound activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the distinct effects in different tissues.

claim: The CNS regulation affects more than one system.
source: Considering the rather broad expression in glial cells, it is furthermore likely that the CNS regulation affects more than one system.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the broad expression pattern.

claim: Localization of Nep4 at the IPC surface supports a direct function in the regulation of dilp expression.
source: However, localization at the IPC surface (Figure 6) clearly supports a direct function in the regulation of dilp expression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization data shown in Figure 6.

claim: IPCs have an allatostatin A receptor (Dar-2), a tachykinin receptor (DTKR), and the short neuropeptide F receptor (sNPFR) at their surface.
source: Such receptors include an allatostatin A receptor (Dar-2) (Hentze et al., 2015), a tachykinin receptor (DTKR) (Birse et al., 2011), and the short neuropeptide F receptor (sNPFR) (Lee et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hentze et al., 2015, Birse et al., 2011, and Lee et al., 2008.

claim: Dar-2, DTKR, and sNPFR are essential to proper dilp expression.
source: All are essential to proper dilp expression (Lee et al., 2008; Hentze et al., 2015; Birse et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2008, Hentze et al., 2015, and Birse et al., 2011.

claim: sNPF ligands (sNPF11–11, sNPF14–11, and sNPF212–19) exhibit very high-binding affinities to sNPFR, with IC50 values in the low nanomolar range.
source: Interestingly, with respect to sNPFR, corresponding ligands (sNPF11–11, sNPF14–11, and sNPF212–19) exhibit very high-binding affinities, with IC50 values in the low nanomolar range (Garczynski et al., 2006), a finding that further emphasizes the need for effective ligand clearance mechanisms in order to prevent inadvertent receptor activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Garczynski et al., 2006.

claim: The high binding affinity of sNPF ligands emphasizes the need for effective ligand clearance mechanisms in order to prevent inadvertent receptor activation.
source: Interestingly, with respect to sNPFR, corresponding ligands (sNPF11–11, sNPF14–11, and sNPF212–19) exhibit very high-binding affinities, with IC50 values in the low nanomolar range (Garczynski et al., 2006), a finding that further emphasizes the need for effective ligand clearance mechanisms in order to prevent inadvertent receptor activation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the high binding affinity.

claim: Localization of Nep4 to the surface of IPCs and confirmation of Dar-2, DTKR, and sNPFR ligands as substrates of the peptidase strongly indicate that Nep4 participates in ligand clearance mechanisms.
source: Localization of Nep4 to the surface of IPCs (Figure 6) and confirmation of Dar-2, DTKR, and sNPFR ligands as substrates of the peptidase (Table 1, Figure 7) strongly indicate that Nep4 participates in such clearance mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization and substrate data.

claim: sNPF species were detected in both CNS and hemolymph preparations, with neuroendocrine functions of the respective peptides being suggested.
source: Of note, sNPF species were detected in both, CNS and hemolymph preparations, with neuroendocrine functions of the respective peptides being suggested (Veenstra et al., 2008; Garczynski et al., 2006; Baggerman et al., 2005; Wegener and Gorbashov, 2008; Wegener et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Both CNS and hemolymph compartments are accessible to Nep4, either to the CNS resident or to the muscle-bound enzyme.
source: The dual localization is interesting because both compartments are accessible to Nep4, either to the CNS resident or to the muscle-bound enzyme.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization data.

claim: sNPF is a potent regulator of dilp expression.
source: Significantly, sNPF is a potent regulator of dilp expression.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge.

claim: Increased sNPF levels result in upregulation of dilp expression, and decreased sNPF levels have the opposite effect.
source: Increased sNPF levels result in upregulation of dilp expression, and decreased sNPF levels have the opposite effect (Lee et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2008.

claim: The effects of modulating sNPF levels inversely correlate with the effects of modulating nep4 expression, suggesting a functional relationship between sNPF and the neprilysin.
source: The fact that these results inversely correlate with the effects of modulating nep4 expression (Figure 3) suggests a functional relationship between sNPF and the neprilysin.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the inverse correlation of effects.

claim: Nep4-mediated cleavage of distinct sNPF species represents further evidence for a functional relationship between sNPF and Nep4.
source: Nep4-mediated cleavage of distinct sNPF species (Table 1, Figure 7) represents further evidence for this relationship.
evidence: This claim is based on mass spectrometry data showing cleavage.

claim: Nep4 cleaves corazonin, drosulfakinins, and allatostatin A.
source: Besides sNPF, Nep4 also cleaves corazonin, drosulfakinins, and allatostatin A (Table 1, Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Table 1 and Figure 7.

claim: Corazonin promotes food intake.
source: Interestingly, corazonin promotes food intake (Hergarden et al., 2012), while allatostatin A and drosulfakinins inhibit it (Hergarden et al., 2012; Söderberg et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hergarden et al., 2012.

claim: Allatostatin A and drosulfakinins inhibit food intake.
source: Interestingly, corazonin promotes food intake (Hergarden et al., 2012), while allatostatin A and drosulfakinins inhibit it (Hergarden et al., 2012; Söderberg et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hergarden et al., 2012, Söderberg et al., 2012, and Chen et al., 2016.

claim: Nep4's regulatory activity on peptides with opposing physiological functions indicates that Nep4 affects multiple aspects of feeding control, rather than promoting or inhibiting food intake in a mutually exclusive manner.
source: This regulatory activity on peptides with opposing physiological functions indicates that Nep4 affects multiple aspects of feeding control, rather than promoting or inhibiting food intake in a mutually exclusive manner.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the substrate diversity.

claim: Both nep4 knockdown and overexpression larvae exhibit reduced food intake.
source: Our finding that both, nep4 knockdown and overexpression larvae exhibit reduced food intake (Figure 3A) supports this indication since it suggests that regular Nep4 activity adjusts the general peptide homeostasis in a manner that promotes optimal food intake, with deviations in either direction being deteriorative.
evidence: This claim is supported by feeding assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Regular Nep4 activity adjusts the general peptide homeostasis in a manner that promotes optimal food intake, with deviations in either direction being deteriorative.
source: Our finding that both, nep4 knockdown and overexpression larvae exhibit reduced food intake (Figure 3A) supports this indication since it suggests that regular Nep4 activity adjusts the general peptide homeostasis in a manner that promotes optimal food intake, with deviations in either direction being deteriorative.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the bidirectional effects on food intake.

claim: nep4 knockdown animals exhibit reduced food intake for only up to 20 min of feeding, which may reflect complex regulation indicating that at the onset of feeding reduced cleavage of peptides inhibiting food intake is a dominant factor.
source: The result that nep4 knockdown animals exhibit reduced food intake for only up to 20 min of feeding (Figure 3A) may reflect this complex regulation since it indicates that at the onset of feeding reduced cleavage of peptides inhibiting food intake (e.g. allatostatin A, drosulfakinins) is a dominant factor.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the temporal pattern of feeding effects.

claim: With ongoing feeding, accumulation of peptides promoting food intake (e.g. corazonin) may become decisive, thus restoring intake rates.
source: With ongoing feeding, accumulation of peptides promoting food intake (e.g. corazonin) may become decisive, thus restoring intake rates.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the mechanism.

claim: Nep4 hydrolyzes numerous peptides that regulate dilp expression, including tachykinins, allatostatin A, and sNPF.
source: In addition, Nep4 hydrolyzes numerous peptides that regulate dilp expression, including tachykinins, allatostatin A, and sNPF.
evidence: This claim is based on mass spectrometry data.

claim: AKH is a functional homolog of vertebrate glucagon that acts antagonistically to insulin.
source: However, AKH, a functional homolog of vertebrate glucagon that acts antagonistically to insulin, is also a substrate of Nep4 (Table 1, Figure 7).
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about AKH function.

claim: AKH is a substrate of Nep4.
source: However, AKH, a functional homolog of vertebrate glucagon that acts antagonistically to insulin, is also a substrate of Nep4 (Table 1, Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Table 1 and Figure 7.

claim: The Nep4-mediated regulation of dilp expression and sugar homeostasis cannot be attributed to a single substrate or cleavage event but is a result of the concerted hydrolysis of several critical peptides.
source: This finding indicates that the Nep4-mediated regulation of dilp expression and sugar homeostasis can also not be attributed to a single substrate or cleavage event. Rather, it is a result of the concerted hydrolysis of several critical peptides, including both, hemolymph circulating and CNS intrinsic factors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the diversity of substrates.

claim: Overexpression and knockdown of nep4 have discrete effects on dilp expression but comparable effects on feeding.
source: Taking into account that overexpression and knockdown of nep4 have discrete effects on dilp expression (Figure 3B), but comparable effects on feeding (Figure 3A), it furthermore appears likely that dysregulation of the Nep4-mediated peptide homeostasis affects both processes somewhat independently of each other.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Dysregulation of the Nep4-mediated peptide homeostasis affects dilp expression and feeding somewhat independently of each other.
source: Taking into account that overexpression and knockdown of nep4 have discrete effects on dilp expression (Figure 3B), but comparable effects on feeding (Figure 3A), it furthermore appears likely that dysregulation of the Nep4-mediated peptide homeostasis affects both processes somewhat independently of each other.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential effects on the two processes.

claim: Among the novel Nep4 substrates, there are peptides that presumably affect either dilp signaling (e.g. DH31), or food intake (e.g. leucokinin, drosulfakinins) in a largely exclusive manner.
source: The fact that among the novel Nep4 substrates we identified peptides that presumably affect either dilp signaling (e.g. DH31), or food intake (e.g. leucokinin, drosulfakinins) in a largely exclusive manner supports this indication.
evidence: This is an inference based on known functions of the substrates.

claim: Neprilysins and many of the novel substrates identified in this study are evolutionarily conserved factors.
source: Because neprilysins and many of the novel substrates identified in this study are evolutionarily conserved factors, neprilysin-mediated regulation of insulin-like peptide expression and feeding behavior may be relevant not only to the energy metabolism in Drosophila, but also to corresponding processes in vertebrates, including humans.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about evolutionary conservation.

claim: Neprilysin-mediated regulation of insulin-like peptide expression and feeding behavior may be relevant to corresponding processes in vertebrates, including humans.
source: Because neprilysins and many of the novel substrates identified in this study are evolutionarily conserved factors, neprilysin-mediated regulation of insulin-like peptide expression and feeding behavior may be relevant not only to the energy metabolism in Drosophila, but also to corresponding processes in vertebrates, including humans.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from evolutionary conservation.

claim: A critical function of murine Neprilysin in determining body mass has been reported.
source: Interestingly, a critical function of murine Neprilysin in determining body mass has already been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about prior findings.

claim: In mice, the regulation of body mass by Neprilysin depended primarily on the catalytic activity of peripheral NEP, while the CNS-bound enzyme was less important.
source: The regulation depended primarily on the catalytic activity of peripheral NEP, while the CNS-bound enzyme was less important (Becker et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Becker et al., 2010.

claim: In Drosophila, mainly peripheral (muscle-bound) Nep4 activity affected body mass, while CNS-specific modulations had only minor effects on size or weight.
source: Our finding that also in Drosophila mainly peripheral (muscle-bound) Nep4 activity affected body mass, while CNS-specific modulations had only minor effects on size or weight (Figure 1), indicates that the neprilysin-mediated regulation of food intake, body size and insulin expression involves similar physiological pathways in both species.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The neprilysin-mediated regulation of food intake, body size and insulin expression involves similar physiological pathways in Drosophila and mice.
source: Our finding that also in Drosophila mainly peripheral (muscle-bound) Nep4 activity affected body mass, while CNS-specific modulations had only minor effects on size or weight (Figure 1), indicates that the neprilysin-mediated regulation of food intake, body size and insulin expression involves similar physiological pathways in both species.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the similarity of effects in both species.

claim: Altered catalytic activity and thus abnormal peptide hydrolysis is a critical factor in both mice and Drosophila.
source: Furthermore, the fact that altered catalytic activity and thus abnormal peptide hydrolysis is a critical factor in mice (Becker et al., 2010) and in Drosophila (Figures 1 and 3) emphasizes the need to generate comprehensive, enzyme-specific lists of neprilysin in vivo substrates.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of findings in both species.

claim: There is a need to generate comprehensive, enzyme-specific lists of neprilysin in vivo substrates.
source: Furthermore, the fact that altered catalytic activity and thus abnormal peptide hydrolysis is a critical factor in mice (Becker et al., 2010) and in Drosophila (Figures 1 and 3) emphasizes the need to generate comprehensive, enzyme-specific lists of neprilysin in vivo substrates.
evidence: This is an inference about future research needs.

claim: The results of the screen for novel Nep4 substrates may be a valuable resource to identify corresponding substrates in vertebrates and humans.
source: In this context, the results of our screen for novel Nep4 substrates (Table 1, Figure 7) may be a valuable resource in order to identify corresponding substrates in vertebrates and humans.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential utility of the findings.
